questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI base unit measures length?
questions.explanation: The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI base unit measures mass?
questions.explanation: The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI base unit measures thermodynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI base unit measures electric current?
questions.explanation: The ampere (A) is the SI base unit of electric current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is the SI base unit of amount of substance?
questions.explanation: The mole (mol) is the SI base unit for amount of substance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is the SI base unit of luminous intensity?
questions.explanation: The candela (cd) is the SI base unit of luminous intensity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is the SI base unit of time?
questions.explanation: The second (s) is the SI base unit of time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression correctly gives the newton in SI base units?
questions.explanation: From F=ma, 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s² = 1 kg m s^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression correctly gives the joule in SI base units?
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement; J = N m = kg m² s^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression correctly gives the watt in SI base units?
questions.explanation: Power = energy/time, so W = J/s = kg m² s^-3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which symbol denotes the SI prefix kilo?
questions.explanation: The SI prefix kilo uses lowercase k and means 10^3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which symbol denotes the SI prefix milli?
questions.explanation: The SI prefix milli is m, meaning 10^-3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which symbol denotes the SI prefix micro?
questions.explanation: Micro is represented by µ and equals 10^-6.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an SI derived unit?
questions.explanation: The pascal is a derived unit of pressure; the others are base units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI unit measures frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), equal to s^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly represents the SI unit symbol for kelvin?
questions.explanation: The symbol is uppercase K without a degree sign.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI unit measures electric charge?
questions.explanation: Charge equals current times time, so the SI unit is coulomb (C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI derived unit measures pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, measured in pascals (Pa).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: How many metres are there in 2.5 km?
questions.explanation: 1 km = 1000 m; therefore 2.5 km = 2500 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Convert 0.075 A into milliamperes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: How many microseconds are there in 3 milliseconds?
questions.explanation: 1 ms = 10^-3 s and 1 µs = 10^-6 s, so 3 ms = 3000 µs.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI base-unit expression equals one pascal?
questions.explanation: Pa = N/m² = (kg m s^-2)/m² = kg m^-1 s^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI base-unit expression equals one coulomb?
questions.explanation: Charge Q = I t, so C = A s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI base-unit expression equals one volt?
questions.explanation: V = J/C = (kg m² s^-2)/(A s) = kg m² s^-3 A^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression gives one ohm in SI base units?
questions.explanation: Ω = V/A = kg m² s^-3 A^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression gives one farad in SI base units?
questions.explanation: F = C/V = (A s)/(kg m² s^-3 A^-1) = kg^-1 m^-2 s^4 A².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A speed of 72 km/h equals how many m/s?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A density of 1 g/cm³ is equal to how many kg/m³?
questions.explanation: 1 g = 10^-3 kg and 1 cm³ = 10^-6 m³, so density is 10³ kg/m³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI derived unit is equivalent to kg m² s^-2?
questions.explanation: The joule equals force times distance: kg m s^-2 × m = kg m² s^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which SI derived unit is equivalent to kg s^-2 A^-1?
questions.explanation: T = N/(A m) = (kg m s^-2)/(A m) = kg s^-2 A^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Express 2.4 × 10^5 µm in metres.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A force of 4 kN acts over an area of 2 m². What is the pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure = 4000 N / 2 m² = 2000 Pa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression represents the SI unit of magnetic flux, weber?
questions.explanation: Wb = V s = kg m² s^-2 A^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 0.50 L volume is how many cubic metres?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of these is the correct SI base-unit expression for momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv, so its unit is kg m s^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A power rating of 2.5 MW equals how many watts?
questions.explanation: Mega means 10^6, so 2.5 MW = 2.5×10^6 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is the SI unit of angular velocity expressed in base units?
questions.explanation: Angular velocity is measured in rad/s; radian is dimensionless, giving s^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which is equal to 1 nanometre?
questions.explanation: Nano denotes 10^-9.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which is the correct SI unit expression for energy density?
questions.explanation: Energy density = J/m³ = kg m² s^-2 /m³ = kg m^-1 s^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 6 m² area equals how many cm²?
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = 10^4 cm² and 6 m² = 60000 cm².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression represents the SI base units of inductance (henry)?
questions.explanation: H = Wb/A = (V s)/A = kg m² s^-2 A^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression gives the SI base units of permittivity ε0?
questions.explanation: From Coulomb's law, ε0 has units C²/(N m²) = (A²s²)/(kg m³ s^-2) = kg^-1 m^-3 s^4 A².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A material has density 8 g/cm³. What is its density in Mg/m³?
questions.explanation: 8 g/cm³ = 8000 kg/m³. Since 1 Mg = 1000 kg, this is 8 Mg/m³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The SI base units of electric field strength are:
questions.explanation: E = force/charge = (kg m s^-2)/(A s) = kg m s^-3 A^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The SI base units of magnetic permeability µ0 are:
questions.explanation: µ0 has units N/A² = kg m s^-2 A^-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A surface energy is 0.08 J/cm². Express it in J/m².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A fluid has dynamic viscosity 2 mPa s. Express it in SI base units.
questions.explanation: 1 Pa s = kg m^-1 s^-1. Milli is 10^-3, hence 2×10^-3 kg m^-1 s^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression gives the SI base units of thermal conductivity?
questions.explanation: From P = k A ΔT/L, k = P L/(A ΔT), giving W m^-1 K^-1 = kg m s^-3 K^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A quantity has units N s/m². Which SI base-unit expression is equivalent?
questions.explanation: N s/m² = (kg m s^-2)s/m² = kg m^-1 s^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is displacement divided by time, so [LT^-1].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity per time, so [LT^-2].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of force?
questions.explanation: F=ma, giving [M][LT^-2]=[MLT^-2].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which physical quantity is dimensionless?
questions.explanation: Strain is the ratio of change in length to original length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass times velocity: [M][LT^-1].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of work?
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance, giving [ML²T^-2].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = [MLT^-2]/[L²] = [ML^-1T^-2].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of the gravitational constant G?
questions.explanation: From F=Gm1m2/r², [G]=[F][L²]/[M²]=[M^-1L³T^-2].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What are the dimensions of power?
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = [ML²T^-3].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If a period T depends only on length l and acceleration g as T ∝ l^a g^b, what are a and b?
questions.explanation: [T]=[L]^a[LT^-2]^b=[L^(a+b)T^(-2b)]. Equating exponents gives b=-1/2 and a=1/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which pair has identical dimensions?
questions.explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum, so both have [MLT^-1].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Dimensions of Young's modulus are
questions.explanation: Young's modulus is stress/strain; strain is dimensionless.

questions.question_text: If T∝ρ^a R^b P^c, where T is time, ρ density, R length and P pressure, find a,b,c
questions.explanation: [ρ]=[ML^-3], [P]=[ML^-1T^-2]. Time requires c=-1/2; mass gives a=1/2; length gives b=1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The difference between a measured value and the accepted reference value is called what?
questions.explanation: Absolute error is the magnitude of the difference between measured and reference values.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression gives relative error?
questions.explanation: Relative error is the absolute error divided by the magnitude of the reference value.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which expression gives percentage error?
questions.explanation: Percentage error is relative error expressed as a percentage.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: How many significant figures are in 0.00450?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant; 4, 5 and the trailing 0 are significant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: How many significant figures are in 6.020?
questions.explanation: The internal zero and the trailing decimal zero are significant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A length is measured as 20.0 ± 0.2 cm. What is its percentage uncertainty?
questions.explanation: Percentage uncertainty = (0.2/20.0)×100 = 1%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A rectangle has length 10.0 ± 0.1 cm and width 5.0 ± 0.1 cm. What is the maximum percentage uncertainty in its area?
questions.explanation: For a product, fractional maximum uncertainties add: 0.1/10 + 0.1/5 = 0.03 = 3%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A quantity z=x² is calculated from x=4.0 ± 0.1. What is the approximate percentage uncertainty in z?
questions.explanation: For z=x², relative uncertainty is approximately 2Δx/x = 2(0.1/4)=5%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A stopwatch records 12.35 s with an absolute uncertainty of 0.05 s. What is the approximate relative uncertainty?
questions.explanation: Relative uncertainty = 0.05/12.35 ≈ 0.00405.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If Q=A²B^-1/2 and the maximum fractional uncertainties in A and B are 2% and 4%, what is the maximum fractional uncertainty in Q?
questions.explanation: For products of powers, maximum fractional uncertainties add with absolute exponents: 2×2% + 0.5×4% = 6%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: How many significant figures are in 0.03040?
questions.explanation: The significant digits are 3, 0, 4 and the final 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: How many significant figures are in 2.500?
questions.explanation: All trailing zeros to the right of a decimal point are significant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which measurement is more precise?
questions.explanation: 2.10 cm is reported to the hundredth of a centimetre, whereas 2.1 cm is to the tenth.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The smallest interval that a measuring instrument can resolve is its:
questions.explanation: Least count is the smallest scale division or resolvable increment.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A consistent offset in every measurement is an example of:
questions.explanation: A persistent offset is systematic rather than random.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which practice primarily reduces random error in an estimated mean?
questions.explanation: Averaging independent repeated readings can reduce the random uncertainty of the mean.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The measured value is 9.8 and the reference value is 10.0. What is the absolute error?
questions.explanation: The absolute difference is |9.8−10.0|=0.2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is 3.14159 rounded to three significant figures?
questions.explanation: The first three significant digits are 3, 1 and 4; the next digit is 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For a reading 5.0 ± 0.1 m, what does ±0.1 m represent?
questions.explanation: The uncertainty is expressed in the same unit as the measured length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A positive zero error in an instrument is generally corrected by:
questions.explanation: A positive zero offset causes an over-reading; subtract it from the observed reading.

questions.explanation: For addition, maximum absolute uncertainties add: 0.2+0.1=0.3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For x=8.0 ± 0.2 and y=3.0 ± 0.1, maximum absolute uncertainty in x−y is:
questions.explanation: For subtraction, maximum absolute uncertainties also add: 0.2+0.1=0.3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A sphere radius is measured with 1% fractional uncertainty. Approximate maximum percentage uncertainty in volume is:
questions.explanation: V∝r³, so percentage uncertainty is approximately 3×1%=3%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A square side is measured with 2% uncertainty. Approximate maximum percentage uncertainty in area is:
questions.explanation: Area∝side², so uncertainty approximately doubles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A value 0.0007080 has how many significant figures?
questions.explanation: The significant digits are 7, 0, 8 and the trailing 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Using the addition rule for decimal places, 12.34+1.2 should be reported as:
questions.explanation: The sum is 13.54, rounded to one decimal place because 1.2 has one decimal place.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Using the multiplication rule for significant figures, 2.4×3.25 should be reported as:
questions.explanation: The product is 7.8; the least precise factor has two significant figures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A vernier caliper has 10 vernier divisions equal to 9 main-scale divisions of 1 mm. Its least count is:
questions.explanation: One vernier division is 0.9 mm; least count = 1−0.9 = 0.1 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A rod length is 25.0 ± 0.1 cm. Approximate percentage uncertainty is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A time interval is measured as 2.00 ± 0.02 s. Percentage uncertainty in its square is approximately:
questions.explanation: For t², fractional uncertainty approximately doubles: 2×(0.02/2.00)×100=2%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For independent readings 6.0 ± 0.2 and 4.0 ± 0.1, the maximum uncertainty in their sum is:
questions.explanation: Worst-case absolute uncertainties add, giving ±0.3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A mass 100.0 ± 0.5 g and volume 20.0 ± 0.2 cm³ yield density with approximate maximum percentage uncertainty:
questions.explanation: For a quotient, percentage uncertainties add: 0.5%+1.0%=1.5%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A value 0.005060 has how many significant figures?
questions.explanation: The significant digits are 5, 0, 6, 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is 8.765 rounded to three significant figures using the usual round-half-up convention?
questions.explanation: Keeping 8.76, the next digit is 5, so the final retained digit rounds up to 7.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A reading is 5.24 cm and an instrument has +0.04 cm zero error. The corrected reading is:
questions.explanation: Corrected reading = observed reading − positive zero error = 5.20 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A screw gauge pitch is 0.5 mm with 50 circular-scale divisions. Its least count is:
questions.explanation: Least count = pitch/number of divisions = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Readings are 10.1, 10.2, 10.3 cm. The mean absolute deviation from the mean is approximately:
questions.explanation: Mean is 10.2 cm; absolute deviations are 0.1, 0, 0.1; mean is 0.2/3≈0.067 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For Q=xy with x=2.0±0.1 and y=5.0±0.2, maximum fractional uncertainty in Q is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For a length 12.0±0.3 cm, which interval is consistent with the stated absolute uncertainty?
questions.explanation: The reported interval is 12.0−0.3 to 12.0+0.3 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If Q=A³B²/C and maximum percentage uncertainties are 1%, 2%, and 3%, maximum percentage uncertainty in Q is:
questions.explanation: Worst-case percentage uncertainty = 3(1%)+2(2%)+3%=10%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The measured radius and height of a cylinder have maximum fractional uncertainties 2% and 3%. Approximate maximum percentage uncertainty in volume is:
questions.explanation: V=πr²h, so ΔV/V≈2Δr/r+Δh/h=4%+3%=7%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A resistance is computed as R=V/I, with V=12.0±0.3 V and I=2.00±0.04 A. Maximum percentage uncertainty in R is:
questions.explanation: Relative uncertainties add: 0.3/12=2.5%, 0.04/2=2%; total 4.5%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A pendulum's period T is determined from 100 oscillations measured in 200.0±0.2 s. Approximate percentage uncertainty in T due to timing is:
questions.explanation: T=t/100; number of oscillations is exact, so fractional uncertainty is 0.2/200=0.1%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If a derived quantity Q=x²/y³, with fractional uncertainties 1.5% in x and 0.5% in y, its maximum percentage uncertainty is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A measured length is 10.00±0.05 cm. What is the approximate maximum percentage uncertainty in its cube?
questions.explanation: Fractional uncertainty in L³ is 3ΔL/L = 3(0.05/10)=1.5%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For z=(a+b)/c, a=4.0±0.1, b=6.0±0.2, c=2.0±0.1, maximum approximate percentage uncertainty in z is:
questions.explanation: Numerator 10.0±0.3 has 3% uncertainty; denominator has 5%; total approximately 8%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cube has side 5.00±0.02 cm. Approximate maximum absolute uncertainty in its volume is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A physical quantity y=kx^(-2), where k is exact and x has 0.8% uncertainty. Approximate percentage uncertainty in y is:
questions.explanation: For a power law, percentage uncertainty is |−2|×0.8%=1.6%.
